scope: Permanent Intel SDK vCPU ownership, retained VM/RAM lifetime, per-call VM clocks, matching checkpoint exclusion and fatal teardown fencing

assumption_register.assumption: Intel vCPU creation, access and destruction must execute on its creating thread.
assumption_register.basis: Retained Apple SDK hv.h/hv_vmx.h ownership contract; prior direct Send handle allowed movement
assumption_register.dependent_result: Movable public facade forwarding to a non-Send core on a permanent worker
assumption_register.stress_test: Move the facade twice, execute and destroy from other callers, use four independent CPU owners, inject constructor/operation/destructor panics
assumption_register.falsification_probe: A substituted SDK callback observes a thread different from the handle creator
assumption_register.status: Confirmed by portable worker tests and actual public backend SDK-substitution fixtures; physical Intel unknown

assumption_register.assumption: An owned CPU returned by Vm::create_vcpu may outlive the public VM wrapper.
assumption_register.basis: Owned Box<dyn VCpu> has no Rust borrow tying its lifetime to Vm; independently observed premature baseline destruction
assumption_register.dependent_result: Shared lifetime retained by every core and facade; final SDK VM destruction after CPU owners join
assumption_register.stress_test: VM dropped first, multiple CPUs dropped on different callers, initialization failure and logical identity reuse
assumption_register.falsification_probe: VM destruction is attempted while a healthy CPU owner remains alive, or registered backing is freed after failed SDK VM destruction
assumption_register.status: Confirmed for the recorded source and SDK model; physical destruction behavior unknown

assumption_register.assumption: Checkpoint exclusion must cover backend-owned operations without recursive acquisition inside a held lease.
assumption_register.basis: CheckpointBoundary ownership contract and existing coordinated runtime hooks
assumption_register.dependent_result: Ordinary request/map/IRQ admission versus stopped capture/restore paths
assumption_register.stress_test: Blocked ordinary read lease, matching/foreign boundary, bounded child capturing and restoring under held write lease
assumption_register.falsification_probe: SDK access occurs through a foreign boundary, or scoped capture/restore hangs waiting on its own read lease
assumption_register.status: Confirmed by actual boundary/lifetime tests and bounded public-backend child; arbitrary external device writers must remain quiescent

assumption_register.assumption: Failed SDK destruction may leave native resources and mappings active.
assumption_register.basis: No undocumented rollback/cleanup-on-error guarantee is assumed
assumption_register.dependent_result: Fence peers/new creation and quarantine mapped backing on failed VM destruction
assumption_register.stress_test: CPU destroy failure, failed initialization cleanup, final VM destroy failure, worker panic
assumption_register.falsification_probe: A peer or new CPU enters SDK after fatal owner loss, or mapping backing drops after failed VM destruction
assumption_register.status: Confirmed in substituted SDK and actual lifetime policy; hardware failure recovery unknown

assumption_register.assumption: Each synchronous owner request must observe the caller VM clock and restore the previous worker binding.
assumption_register.basis: Explicit TimingContext contract; worker threads do not inherit caller thread-local state
assumption_register.dependent_result: Clock binding inside each request closure
assumption_register.stress_test: Nested caller clocks with distinct public diagnostic counters and subsequent unbound call
assumption_register.falsification_probe: SDK callback sees another VM diagnostic counter or retains a prior request clock
assumption_register.status: Confirmed by public SDK-boundary fixture; native retirement/TSC scheduling remains open

change_surface.backend: Intel facade/core split, owner transport, VM/RAM lifetime, request clocks, checkpoint exclusion and teardown
change_surface.CPU_state: Existing public architectural projection preserved; complete native private/XSAVE context is not added by this group
change_surface.machine_devices: Existing IRQ queue/mapping semantics retained and fenced by VM exclusion; full routing/conservation remains open
unaffected: C ABI layout and C API software engines

baseline.caveat: Combined baseline reproduces premature VM destruction; its later movement case was obscured by fixture mutex poisoning. The separate fresh-process movement run is the valid owner-thread counterexample. Fixture poisoning was repaired before green runs.

validation.scope: Actual Intel backend with all SDK symbols substituted; no hardware VM/guest instruction. Portable owner/lifetime policies run separately.
validation.iteration_failure: owner-green-v1 failed to compile because the test used a private clock accessor; it provides no runtime result. The fixture now observes public diagnostic counters.
validation.profile: Green/final: debug assertions and overflow checks enabled, test optimization level 1, LTO off. Exact final environment and commands retained. Baseline profile differs as recorded; no hardware/code-generation conformance is inferred.

baseline_profile.LTO: initial inherited/default setting; LLVM ThinLTO activity was sampled
baseline_profile.provenance: Known per-command overrides reconstructed from the executed baseline driver; its complete inherited environment was not separately captured

validation.complete_check_scope: Workspace all-target check/build/clippy with C API JIT feature; Intel debug and no-debug library type checks; complete selected backend binaries without test-name filters. No current-source full root-library or C API runtime result is inferred.

bounded_scope.finding: Complete native XSAVE/private/in-flight serialization and coordinated restoration remain required. The existing architectural projection still omits SIMD/private state.
Native bounded scheduling, complete interrupt/device conservation, remaining MMIO/MSR/intercept profiles and physical Intel VMX qualification remain required.
The guest CPUID/XSAVE profile is static; host capability admission and full advertised-state capture remain required alongside private-state serialization.
SDK failure recovery is modeled; actual kernel teardown/rollback behavior has not been executed on physical Intel.
The SDK-substitution executable requires Intel macOS code. Running it through Rosetta validates the listed Rust/SDK-boundary behavior, not hardware virtualization.

Cold Intel fixture baseline code generation took approximately 647 seconds under host memory pressure; sampled LLVM ThinLTO was active. Local LTO-off validation avoids repeating that optimization; no global profile was changed.
Only the existing integration checkout and canonical build/scratch roots are used. Build roots are removed after the tested commit.

full_goal: A32-FP/C-STATE/C-SMP/C-HVF remain incomplete; no audit finding status is promoted by this component group.
